title: Encapsulate Variable

solutions.title: Named functions, not a shared object
solutions.tradeoff: Eight small functions where there were five raw fields, and a fifth caller could no longer add itself without one. Every future setting needs its own accessor written by hand - a general get/set pair would have been cheaper to extend and is exactly what this solution gives up.

reviewFocus: Is `settings` still reachable from outside `club-settings.ts` - by import, not just by convention? Encapsulate Variable is not finished while any sibling file can still write a field directly.

Does `club-settings.ts` export a general `getClubSettings()` / `setClubSettings()` pair, or specific functions like `spotsRemaining()` and `admitOneMember()`? Either is a legitimate reading of the move - what does each cost the next field that gets added?

If a getter still hands back the live `settings` object, would a caller assigning into the result compile? A `readonly` field stops that at the type level; check whether that is being relied on, or whether nothing actually stops it.

`decideEntry` reads `spotsRemaining()` and then, on the same call, changes it. Encapsulating the variable did not remove that coupling - it only gave it a name. Is that still in scope for this refactoring, or is it the next one?
`startSeason` resets `memberCount` as a side effect of configuring dues and capacity. Is that one function doing two jobs, or one seasonal reset that happens to touch five fields at once?
